newsitem.title: UK: IBCA sees no MG impact on Deutsche rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA sees no MG impact on Deutsche rating.

text.p: IBCA, the European rating agency, does not see the situation regarding Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) as having a decisive implication for Deutsche Bank AG's AAA rating, IBCA managing director Robin Monro-Davies said on Monday.
"An event like this is not the sort of thing which we would change a rating for," Monro-Davies told Reuters in an interview.

He said the type of events which are decisive are those which show endemic poor control or involve sums so large they weakened the institution. "Neither of those criteria can be applied to this particular event," he said.
Earlier on Monday, a Moody's Investors Service banking analyst said the agency was looking at the implications for Deutsche Bank's ratings from the situation regarding MGAM.

"I can tell you we are looking at the situation," Samuel Theodore, Moody's managing director for European financial institutons, told Reuters. He said the rating agency's analysis was "in the general context of the rating for the group".
Deutsche Bank currently has an Aaa rating from Moody's and is one of the few triple-A rated banks in the world.
Deutsche Bank said on Monday that MGAM had enough cash to cover fund outflows.

Trading in three of its funds was temporarily halted last week due to "irregularities". The manager of two of the funds, Peter Young, has been suspeneded and his personal assets frozen pending a probe into his management of the funds.
Salomon Brothers said in a research note on Monday that Deutsche's expansion into global investment banking highlighted its vulnerability to a credit downgrade.
"A rapid expansion into global investment banking has already raised Deutsche Bank's risk profile and, by extension, its vulnerability to a credit downgrade," the research note said.
